How we screen CVs

Recruiters spend about seven seconds on the first pass, so put the role title and the last employer where the eye lands first.

What we look for

  • Quantify the outcome: a number beats an adjective, on every bullet.
  • Keep the CV to one page per ten years of experience, no more.
  • Write the acronym and its full name the first time it appears.
  • Start each line with the verb, not with the role you held.

What slows a CV down

Avoid tables and multi-column layouts: the parser reads them out of order and the result looks like nonsense to whoever opens it next.

Use the same date format everywhere; mixed formats make the sort unreliable.
